summary: Zaca Peak pole-tower lookout, Santa Barbara County, CA: built 1914, replaced by Figueroa Mountain and removed in 1917; no source describes the site now.

facts.design: crude 25-foot pole tower with a canvas-roofed platform
facts.status_note: Removed in 1917 according to the register; the station moved to Figueroa Mountain
facts.agency: US Forest Service, Los Padres National Forest

access.note: Forest land around Zaca Lake is open to the public and a trail reaches Zaca Peak. No source describes the old site itself.

visit.trail_note: Zaca Peak via Grass Mountain Loop Trail is a strenuous 8.8-mile hike; the route can be a bit tricky to follow without a good map

events.note: January 1916 Santa Maria Times item, reprinted on the Forest Lookouts page, refers to the lookout man at Zaca Mountain
Register says Figueroa Mountain replaced the site as primary; a July 1917 item reports the station moved
Registered April 16, 2020; nominated by Brad Eells

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates removal to 1917 and says Figueroa Mountain replaced the site. A July 1917 newspaper item says the station moved there. Both put the change in 1917, so the story treats them as one event.

notes_for_editor: Record's built 1914 and gone status hold. Access rests on a Santa Maria Times column about Zaca Lake and its trail, not a survey of the summit, so access is public with a caveat. No source describes remains on the peak. Figueroa Mountain, the 1917 successor site, is not covered here.
